root.name: Colle System: Rhamphorhynchus Variation
root.moves: 1. Nf3 c5 2. e3 g6 3. d4 Bg7 4. dxc5 Qa5+

overview: White uses a Colle-style set-up against a Sicilian-style Black. After 3.d4 Bg7 4.dxc5 Qa5+ Black regains the c5 pawn with the queen check, then develops the g7 bishop and knights. The result is a quiet game with a fianchetto for Black and an e3 structure for White.

white_ideas.idea: Develop with Nc3, Bd2 or Nbd2 and take back c5
Play e3 and Bd3 to develop
Aim for a space edge with e4

black_ideas.idea: Play for ...d5 or ...b6 depending on set-up

typical_structures.structure: White e3 pawn structure against Black fianchetto
Open c-file after c5 pawn trade

character.notes: A calm opening with little forcing play.

gambit.notes: No material is given up in the main line.

soundness.notes: Black regains the pawn at once; White is comfortable.

structure.notes: After pawns come off the centre it is mostly pieces, and the structure stays open to change.

approach.notes: A rare line whose name is more famous than play; used by some for variety.

level.notes: Few lines, but placement of pieces takes sense.

character.reason: Neither side takes on much risk and play is calm.

gambit.reason: The c5 pawn is regained at once.

structure.reason: The centre is still undecided after dxc5 and pieces decide.

approach.reason: A rarer sideline but not a surprise weapon only.

level.reason: Plans are straightforward but need judgement.

plans.reason: Black fianchettoes and the queen comes out early with check.
